question: Why must swimmers in most strokes surface within 15 m of the start and each turn?
answer: Because underwater is faster. A body submerged by about a metre escapes the surface waves that make up much of a swimmer's drag. At the 1988 Olympics David Berkoff and others kicked most of a backstroke length underwater; the sport capped it at 10 m that year, and settled on 15 m in 1991.
